ch01.card: Part 1 of 8. One question, start to finish.
ch01.s01.c1: This part follows one question through the whole model.
ch01.s01.c2: The model has five parts: reader, thinker, calculator, stop switch and talker.
ch01.s01.c3: Some parts have a test result. But all five together have never been tested.
ch01.s02.c1: Here is the question. We made it up as an example.
ch01.s02.c2: The model works on letters, so every letter gets its own box.
ch01.s02.c3: The question has 71 characters, spaces included.
ch01.s03.c1: A borrowed reader, trained by someone else, reads the whole question once. Its name is EmbeddingGemma 2.
ch01.s03.c2: Frozen means our practice, which we call training, never changes it.
ch01.s03.c3: Each letter gets 768 numbers from the reader. They are the numbers of the word piece the letter sits in.
ch01.s03.c4: The reader has 271,002,624 numbers. We did not set them.
ch01.s04.c1: A small learned window lets each letter see 4 letters on each side.
ch01.s04.c2: It is ours, learned from scratch in our practice.
ch01.s04.c3: In small tests at the 3 million size, every reader without it failed the letter-code puzzles.
ch01.s05.c1: The thinker is the part that loops. One lap around the question is one round.
ch01.s05.c2: In each round it looks at the whole question, passes notes, and thinks.
ch01.s05.c3: The same learned settings are used every round. Only its notes change.
ch01.s06.c1: In round 1 the thinker looks at every letter and passes notes.
ch01.s06.c2: No call is written after round 1, so the call slot stays empty. A call is a request to the calculator.
ch01.s06.c3: In the version we tested, the first call comes after round 2.
ch01.s07.c1: After round 2 the call writer reads the thinker's first control vector, which is a list of numbers.
ch01.s07.c2: It picks one of 8 operations, or writes no call. No call is a choice.
ch01.s07.c3: The 8 are add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max and cmp.
ch01.s08.c1: The numbers are copied, not typed. A learned pointer finds the last digit of each number.
ch01.s08.c2: The code copies one letter at a time to the left, until the learned stop head says stop.
ch01.s08.c3: Some steps are still hand-written code, like flipping the digits into reading order.
ch01.s09.c1: The calculator is an ordinary program. It is outside the model.
ch01.s09.c2: The model writes its request as text, and gets the answer back as text.
ch01.s09.c3: With the calculator switched off, questions that need a calculation scored 0.0 points out of 100 on all 6 copies.
ch01.s10.c1: The calculator gets sub 12 5 and sends back 7, as plain text.
ch01.s10.c2: As built, the letter window reads the reply, not the Gemma reader. The calculator and Gemma have never run together.
ch01.s10.c3: The question is not read again. The reply goes into the notes.
ch01.s11.c2: The call writer writes add 7 3. The 7 is from the reply, and the 3 is from the question.
ch01.s11.c3: The calculator returns 10, and add 7 3 = 10 joins the notes.
ch01.s12.c1: Some rounds have nothing to calculate, so they write no call.
ch01.s12.c2: In the version we tested, calls come after rounds 2 to 8 only.
ch01.s12.c3: The newest version can call in any round from 2 to 32. It is built, but not tested.
ch01.s13.c1: After each round a small learned switch asks: is it done yet?
ch01.s13.c2: It must run at least 1 round, and at most 32. The 32 is a safety limit.
ch01.s13.c3: One stop covers the whole answer. It is built, but never tested yet.
ch01.s14.c1: The talker copies 10 from the last reply, where the thinker points.
ch01.s14.c2: It adds no thinking of its own, so the answer is just the copied 10.
ch01.s14.c3: Today's talker is a stand-in. The English talker, about 25 million numbers, is planned.
ch01.s15.c1: Green. Adding the Gemma reader gained 2.67 points out of 100 on 6,040 questions, in 6 of 6 copies, at 3M.
ch01.s15.c2: Green. The calculator outside matched the old calculator-inside model in 6 copies. One check on no-thinking answers missed, but the project owner cleared it.
ch01.s15.c3: Amber: calls in any round, and the stop switch. Built, never tested.
ch01.s15.c4: Grey: the English talker. A placeholder, not built yet.
ch01.s15.c5: Open question: with the Gemma reader, some answers use zero thinking rounds. All five together: never tested.
ch01.s16.c1: The reader reads once. The thinker thinks in rounds. The calculator does the sums.
ch01.s16.c2: The stop switch says when done. The talker writes the answer.
ch01.s16.c3: Now we open each box, one at a time.
